source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Phyllostictose / Phyllosticta leaf spot (caused by Phyllosticta species) causes discrete leaf spotting similar in general appearance to Septoria leaf spot, and the source notes it is likewise a fungal infection favored by humid conditions that spreads through airborne and rain-splashed spores.

As with the other citrus leaf-spotting fungal diseases in this source, the practical impact is mainly a reduction in leaf area and tree vigor when infection is heavy, rather than a disease that directly destroys fruit.

Control measures mirror those for Septoria and other leaf-spot fungi: sanitation (removing infected fallen leaves), pruning for better air circulation, and protective copper fungicide sprays during the rainy season when conditions favor infection.
